newsitem.title: FRANCE: French far-right leader to attend Pope rally.
newsitem.headline: French far-right leader to attend Pope rally.

text.p: France's far-right leader Jean-Marie Le Pen said he plans to attend Pope John Paul's celebration of the 1,500th anniversary of the baptism of pagan king Clovis in the northeast cathedral city of Reims on Sunday.

"Some people think the country, the nation, history, all that is not important, that we are French because we live here or because we just happened to be born here," Le Pen, under fire for saying races are unequal, told France-3 television in a Sunday evening interview.

"I believe in the past, I believe in roots, I am proud of belonging to an ancient country...I will therefore be where the Pope will be, among the deputies because I am a European (Parliament) deputy," he said.
Le Pen said he would go to Reims to honour the head of the Roman Catholic Church, who will visit France for three days from Thursday, and to honour 1,500 years of French history.

Clovis, a pagan king who was the first west European monarch to convert to Roman Catholicism, has been hijacked as a symbol of the National Front. It says white, Christian French civilisation is superior to others.

Mainstream politicians have savaged Le Pen for saying racial differences are "a fact". But almost all shied away from proposals to ban his party, fearing a backlash of sympathy for his anti-immigrant views.
